statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 17 of 100 in the low band, eight points below the 25 block threshold, while stress eases further to 77 in the high band and confidence holds at 88.
recommendation: Tail sits in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The decisive evidence remains the observed price path, which has stayed orderly through the afternoon: the 29,499.50 high has capped NQ for roughly six hours, price rotates about 80 points beneath it, and the cash index has faded 74 points from its own intact 29,473.12 high. A market that keeps retracing inside a 461-point range under a fixed ceiling is granting mean reversion rather than denying it, so neither the closing auction nor the Friday weekly expiry is treated as observed one-way structure. The named window covers 19:00 to 21:00 UTC, spanning the final cash hour into the 20:00 UTC close and the thin post-close hour before the 21:00 UTC weekend halt, where conditional tail peaks at 17 and stays inside the low band throughout. From 21:00 UTC the remainder of the horizon lies entirely inside the CME weekend closure, so conditional tail falls to a 5 to 7 floor that represents residual model uncertainty rather than any live structure. Stress remains in the high band because the Hormuz disruption, crude above 100 dollars and an FOMC decision priced close to a 25 basis point increase are all unresolved, but under this repository's fixed mapping stress alone does not move the published policy state.
headline: Rotation holds beneath an intact ceiling into the Friday close: NQ trades near 29,420.25 about 80 points under a 29,499.50 session high that has capped price for roughly six hours, NDX is 29,399.51 and 1.02% higher but 74 points below its own 29,473.12 high, VIX is 15.92 after basing at 15.59, and WTI is 100.55 and 1.9% lower as Gulf-Iran talks on the Strait of Hormuz are reported for Monday.
body:
Both dated U.S. releases for Friday are verified and behind the market. The Bureau of Labor Statistics published the August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC: all items rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% over twelve months, while all items less food and energy rose 0.3% on the month, a tenth above consensus, and 2.4% over the year. Gasoline rose 3.9% and accounted for over a third of the monthly all-items increase. The University of Michigan preliminary September survey followed at 14:00 UTC at 47.8 against a 51.0 consensus and a 51.7 August final, with year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.6% and the longer-run measure at 3.4%.

The price path remains the decisive evidence and it continues to grant mean reversion. NQ futures trade near 29,420.25, roughly 80 points below a 29,499.50 session high that has now capped the contract for about six hours, inside a 461-point range measured from the 29,040.50 low. The cash index at 29,399.51 is 1.02% higher on the day yet 74 points under its own 29,473.12 high, which is likewise unbroken. Repeated retracement beneath a fixed ceiling is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure that defines tail risk, so tail stays in the low band at 17 even as the final cash hour and the Friday weekly-expiry auction concentrate closing flow.

Cross-asset evidence is mixed rather than aligned. VIX is 15.92, down about 10.8% on the day, having based at 15.59 and ticked up modestly into the close from a 17.71 high. Treasury yields are higher but orderly, with the 10-year near 4.975% after a roughly 3 basis point rise and the 2-year at 4.63% after about 4 basis points, a modest bear-flattening consistent with firmer near-term policy pricing. Crude eased, with WTI at 100.55 and Brent at 104.97 after declines of 1.9% and 2.5%, on reports that Oman is seeking to convene Gulf Cooperation Council foreign ministers and Iran in Salalah on Monday to discuss passage through the Strait of Hormuz. Delayed latest-session context shows all eight tracked megacaps higher with a mean gain near 1.16% and six of seven tracked semiconductors higher with a mean near 1.91%, supported by Oracle's fiscal first quarter, in which cloud infrastructure revenue rose 121% to 7.4 billion dollars with a 664 billion dollar backlog. That breadth is supportive of direction but is not live price-path evidence and is not used as such.

Forward risk is concentrated well beyond this horizon. CME equity-index futures halt at 21:00 UTC for the weekend and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so twenty-two of the twenty-four forecast slots contain no tradable price path at all. The verified seven-day calendar is dominated by the 15 to 16 September FOMC meeting, which carries a Summary of Economic Projections and a press conference, alongside August Retail Sales on the same morning. Reporting after Friday's inflation data put the probability of a 25 basis point increase near 86 to 87%, up from roughly 60 to 72% earlier in the week, which is the principal reason stress remains in the high band while tail does not.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 19:00 UTC on 10 September to 18:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 17 with the mode mixed, then records event/whipsaw readings of 19 and 18 across the 20:00 and 21:00 UTC slots around the previous cash close. The overnight hours from 22:00 UTC ease steadily to a low of 11 as Asian and early European trade stayed orderly, and the mode turns trend-up from 06:00 UTC through 11:00 UTC as the European session built a directional advance without denying retracement. The only elevated readings in the window are 21 and 22 in the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots, both marked event/whipsaw and both in the watch band around the 12:30 UTC consumer price release, where confidence also fell to 70 and 80 while the outcome was still being absorbed. From 14:00 UTC the series returns to the low band at 15 with the mode mixed and stays there for the final five hours at 15, 16, 15, 15 and 15, while stress declines monotonically from 82 to 78. No lookback value has been revised with information that was unavailable when it was published.
outlookSummary: The forward window contains roughly two hours of tradable session and then spends its remaining twenty-two slots inside the CME weekend closure that begins at 21:00 UTC. Conditional tail opens at 17 in the current slot, the only slot that contains observed rather than hypothetical structure, covering the final cash hour, the Friday weekly-expiry auction and the 20:00 UTC close. It eases to 15 for the post-close hour on the assumption that expiry unwind releases rather than extends directional pressure, then drops to 7 as the weekend halt takes effect and settles on a 5 to 6 floor for every remaining hour. That floor is residual model uncertainty, not a forecast of structure, because a persistent no-retracement price path cannot form while the contract is not trading. Stress declines from 77 through 73 and 60 to a weekend baseline near 32, and confidence decays gradually from 88 to 68 purely as a function of distance from the Friday evidence cutoff rather than any weakness in the evidence gathered. Every forecast slot maps to EA_ON and green. Material weekend developments, including the Gulf-Iran meeting reported for Monday in Salalah, would express themselves as a gap at the 22:00 UTC Sunday reopen, which falls outside this horizon and is therefore excluded from every tail value published here.
